What would most likely be considered an advantage by producers and a disadvantage by consumers of the operation of a planned economy?

options.A: a bureaucratic system of decision-making
options.B: a government emphasis on the production of capital goods
options.C: a long response time to changing economic events
options.D: an absence of financial incentives to work and to produce

questions.questionText: A country can produce manufactured goods and agricultural products as shown in the diagram. agricultural V products T S Q R O manufactured goods Given this information, which statement is definitely correct?

options.A: If the country produces at Q it has unused or inefficiently used resources.
options.B: The country should produce at T instead of at Q.
options.C: The country would be better off producing at R than S.
options.D: The monetary costs are the same to produce at V as they are to produce at R.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a demand curve for a good. price D O quantity Which statement describes the nature of this demand curve?

options.A: A greater or smaller quantity is demanded as price changes.
options.B: A lower price is the result of a fall in demand.
options.C: As demand increases so does price.
options.D: Quantity changes in proportion to the change in price.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between the price and the total expenditure on a good. price O total expenditure Which statement is correct?

options.A: The income elasticity of demand for the commodity is unity.
options.B: The income elasticity of demand for the commodity is zero.
options.C: The price elasticity of demand for the commodity is unity.
options.D: The price elasticity of demand for the commodity is zero.

questions.questionText: Over the last ten years the price elasticity of demand for tea in many countries has risen. What is the most likely cause of this change in price elasticity?

options.A: a decrease in the incomes of consumers
options.B: a decrease in the number of complements to tea
options.C: an increase in the amount of tea supplied
options.D: an increase in the number of substitutes for tea

questions.questionText: What would be the price elasticity of supply of cell (mobile) phones if their price rose from US$100 to US$110 and the quantity supplied rose from 200 to 250?
A product has a high price elasticity of supply. What might explain this?

options.A: The product has a high opportunity cost.
options.B: The product has a non-perishable nature.
options.C: The product is classed as an inferior good.
options.D: The product is considered to be a luxury.

options.A: On a demand and supply diagram for houses there has been a movement up the demand curve.
options.B: On a demand and supply diagram for houses there has been a movement up the supply curve.
options.C: The price elasticity of demand for houses is greater than one.
options.D: The price elasticity of supply of houses is zero.

questions.questionText: Which statement about maximum and minimum prices is correct?

options.A: With an effective maximum price for a product, a shortage will develop.
options.B: With an effective maximum price for a product, the market price will rise.
options.C: With an effective minimum price for a product, rationing will be necessary.
options.D: With an effective minimum price for a product, the market price will fall.

Why are the pensions paid to retired citizens an example of a transfer payment?

options.A: Retired citizens pay no tax on their pensions.
options.B: Retired citizens produce no output for their pensions.
options.C: Retired citizens save some of their pensions.
options.D: Retired citizens spend all of their pensions.

questions.questionText: What is definitely a feature of a nationalised industry?

options.A: Consumers are not charged a price for its product.
options.B: No profit is made from supplying its product.
options.C: The government owns the industry’s capital.
options.D: There is no competition in the market for its product.

questions.questionText: Which government action would be identified as the direct provision of goods and services?

options.A: increasing road maintenance because of poor weather conditions
options.B: making payments to low-income families with elderly dependants
options.C: subsidising firms in order to encourage them to increase their output
options.D: taxing firms because they have been emitting damaging fumes

questions.questionText: What would be certain to cause a fall in a country’s cost of living?

options.A: a fall in real incomes
options.B: a fall in the inflation rate
options.C: a negative inflation rate
options.D: a reduction in direct tax rates

questions.questionText: A newspaper headline stated that the Australian car industry has been affected by the strength of the Australian dollar. What would not be an effect caused by a strong rising Australian dollar?

options.A: Reduced foreign demand for Australian cars caused increased unemployment.
options.B: The price of exports of Australian cars became more expensive.
options.C: The price of foreign competitive cars became less expensive.
options.D: The price of imports of car parts became more expensive.
